text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Members of parliament discuss Lebanon pullout.
- Labour party's Ehud Barak: I proposed deal to leave Lebanon when foreign minister.
- Government declares Bezeq services "vital," limiting private ownership.
- 23 Palestinian women prisoners to be released this week. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi request pardon for Jewish murderers of Arabs.
- Scientists at Israel's Weizmann Institute discover gene which could help fight AIDS.
HAARETZ
- Air force chief will announce temporary change in flight procedures, until inquiry completes its report.
- One of the helicopters was supposed to take another group of soldiers into Lebanon the same night.
- Sunday Times: Syrian leader Hafez al-Assad was unconscious for two weeks; Russian doctors saved him.
- Tonight a summit between Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
- Sources in prosecutor's office: There will be a need to investigate Netanyahu in the attorney-general affair.
MAARIV
- Koor and Blue Square real estate company to set up shopping mall in Jordanian capital.
- Netanyahu will give cabinet ministers the basics of his final-status proposal in territories this week.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Government decides Bezeq to remain under Israeli control.
- Effort to return Palestinian workers to building sector.
- Expectation: January cost-of-living high, a rise of 0.5 to 0.6 percent. Record dollar = 3.326 shekels. Big chance stock exchange will fall this week.
- Inquiry examines series of failures on flights. One of the pilots had disease that might have caused heart attack.
